title: Remaping shift(right) to shift(left) will make shift(right) locked after using it.

status.label: Investigate stuck Shift state after remapping
status.detail: The report says mapping Right Shift to Left Shift leaves the original Right Shift state stuck until the mapping is removed and Right Shift is pressed again; an identical report #42057 is closed as a duplicate.

judgment.rationale: The report gives a concrete modifier-to-modifier mapping and state transition: Right Shift to Left Shift causes Right Shift to remain pressed when used with another key, and removing the mapping then pressing Right Shift clears the state. A second report, #42057, describes the same mapping and stuck-key behavior and is closed with state reason DUPLICATE; no linked fix or pull request is recorded. This supports a focused fix investigation, although the original report lists PowerToys 0.94.2 and has no current-stable retest.
evidence: The report lists PowerToys 0.94.2 on Windows 11 with a Traditional Chinese input environment.
The mapping is Right Shift to Left Shift; using Right Shift with another key leaves Right Shift stuck in a pressed state.
Removing the mapping and pressing Right Shift again clears the stuck state.
Issue #42057 describes the same mapping and stuck-key behavior and is closed as a duplicate; it has no linked pull request.
judgment.recommended_action: Confirm the same modifier-state failure on current stable, then trace key-down/key-up balancing when one Shift key is remapped to the other.

fix_assessment.rationale: The mapping and recovery sequence point to an unbalanced synthetic/original modifier state. A fix should be investigated in the key-event handling path, but the exact state transition has not been traced.

proposed_fixes.title: Balance Right Shift state for modifier-to-modifier remaps
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The Right Shift key-up state may not be balanced when the remap emits Left Shift, leaving the original modifier logically pressed until another physical event clears it.
plan: Reproduce Right Shift to Left Shift on current stable and record the Right Shift and Left Shift down/up sequence.
Trace the Keyboard Manager path that emits the replacement modifier and releases the original key.
If the original Right Shift release is missing or delayed, correct the remap path so both physical and synthesized modifier state are balanced on key-up and on mapping removal.
Add regression coverage for Right Shift to Left Shift while typing, releasing the modifier, and removing the mapping.
verification: Right Shift to Left Shift behaves as Left Shift without leaving either Shift key logically pressed.
The behavior remains correct across repeated key presses and modifier release.
Removing the mapping does not require an extra physical key press to clear modifier state.

confidence.rationale: The stuck state and recovery behavior are explicit and a matching duplicate report supports the symptom, but the actual key-event sequence and current-version status have not been independently confirmed.
